{{Infobox election | election_name = United States House of Representatives election in Wyoming, At-large district, 2018 | country = Wyoming | type = presidential | ongoing = no | previous_election = United States House of Representatives election in Wyoming, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives election in Wyoming, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | election_date = {{Start date|2018|11|06}} | image1 = [[File:Liz Cheney 15800286.jpg|150x150px]] | nominee1 = [[Liz Cheney]] | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = [[File:Greg Hunter at Campbell County League of Women Voters' General Election Candidates' Forum in Gillette, Wyoming (cropped).jpg|x150px]] | nominee2 = Greg Hunter | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Liz Cheney]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{ElectionsWY}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives election in Wyoming''' will be held on November 6, 2018 to elect the [[U.S. Representative]] from [[Wyoming's at-large congressional district]], who will represent the state of Wyoming in the [[116th United States Congress]]. The election coincides with the [[United States elections, 2016|2018 U.S. mid-term elections]], as well as [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2018#State elections|state]] and [[United States elections, 2018#Local elections|local elections]]. Key [[Wyoming elections, 2018|2018 races in Wyoming]] include elections for [[Wyoming gubernatorial election, 2018|Governor]], [[Wyoming elections, 2018#Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] of [[Wyoming Secretary of State|Wyoming]], [[United States Senate election in Wyoming, 2018|U.S. Senate]], 15 of the 30 seats in the [[Wyoming State Senate]], and all 60 seats in the [[Wyoming House of Representatives]]. Going into the 2018 U.S. House election, Republican [[Liz Cheney]] is the [[Incumbent|incumbent]] and is seeking reelection.{{cite web|url=http://cheneyforwyoming.com/|title=Cheney for Wyoming|accessdate=August 1, 2018}} Primary elections to determine each party's nominee for the general election were held on August 21, 2018.{{cite web|url=http://soswy.state.wy.us/Elections/2018ElectionInformation.aspx|title=2018 Election Information|website=[[Wyoming Secretary of State]]|publisher=Wyoming Secretary of State’s Office|accessdate=August 1, 2018}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== *[[Liz Cheney]], incumbent, daughter of former Vice President [[Dick Cheney]], and candidate for the U.S. Senate in [[United States Senate election in Wyoming, 2014|2014]]{{cite web|url=http://cheneyforwyoming.com/|title=Cheney for Wyoming|accessdate=August 1, 2018}} *Rod Miller, cowboy{{cite web|url=http://millerforwyoming.com/|title=Rod Miller for Wyoming from Wyoming|accessdate=August 1, 2018}} *Blake E. Stanley{{cite web|url=https://www.wyomingnews.com/news/local_news/blake-stanley-enters-race-for-wyoming-s-u-s-house/article_b198c3a0-6a16-11e8-ae34-9f18d2b45302.html|title=Blake Stanley enters race for Wyoming's U.S. House seat|publisher=[[Wyoming Tribune Eagle]]||last=Funk|first=Joel|date=June 7, 2018|accessdate=August 1, 2018}} ===Results=== [[File:2018 WY-AL Republican primary.svg|thumb|Results by county: {{legend|#aa0000|Cheney—80–90%}} {{legend|#d40000|Cheney—70–80%}} {{legend|#ff0000|Cheney—60–70%}} {{legend|#ff2a2a|Cheney—50–60%}} {{legend|#ff5555|Cheney—40–50%}} ]] {{Election box begin no change | title = Republican primary results{{cite web|url=http://soswy.state.wy.us/Elections/ElectionResults.aspx|title=Election Results|publisher=[[Wyoming Secretary of State]]|accessdate=August 1, 2018}}}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Liz Cheney]] [[Incumbent|(incumbent)]] | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 75,183 | percentage = 63.7 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Rod Miller | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 22,045 | percentage = 18.7 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Blake E.
